text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- The Swiss government proposed to the parliament a credit of 18 million Swiss francs for the next five years to promote Swiss tourism projects.
- Swiss radio and television will be broadcast via satelite. The Swiss Broadcasting Company won government permission.

- Swiss President Flavio Cotti will today sign the Partnership for Peace treaty at the Nato headquarters in Brussels, Belgium. - Swiss economy was still sluggish in the third quarter 1996 as the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) shrunk by 0.7 percent compared to the previous quarter.
- The Swiss government decided yesterday to cut total salaries to public employees by 309 million Swiss francs.
- The lower house of Swiss parliament decided to adopt the so-called 'mini slaughter plan', which inlcudes the killing of some 1,000 cows to eradicate the mad cow disease in Switzerland.
Originally, the government planned to slaughter 230,000 cows.
- Swiss Re to take over Italian reinsurance company Unione Italiana di Riassicurazione for 500 million Swiss francs.
- Swiss machine group Maag said that it expected a 1996 net profit of two million Swiss francs after a loss of 49.5 million francs in the previous year.

- The Swiss government granted 365 million Swiss francs for a export risk guarantee for two Swiss technology groups Sulzer and ABB, who both will deliver parts to build a huge hydro-electric power plant in China.
